question.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ All triangles are not acute.
question.worked_solution:
Let $T$ be the set of all triangles. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ For all $x\in T,$ $x$ is not acute.

Introducing the universal quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∀x\in T,\,x\text{ is not acute}.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀x\in T,\,x\text{ is not acute}) & ≡∃x\in T,\,¬(x\text{ is not acute}) \\  & ≡∃x\in T,\,x\text{ is acute}\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ There exists $x\in T$ such that $x$ is acute.

or simply

$\,$ Some triangles are acute.
